judge_reasoning: The model's solution incorrectly assumes Mirage Mirror retains its own copy-ability after already becoming a copy of Multiform Wonder. Per the copy-effect rules, once Mirage Mirror fully resolves as a copy of another permanent, it loses its own printed abilities (including its own copy-changing ability) and only has the copied object's abilities. The official solution requires activating both copy abilities simultaneously (stacked, before either resolves) specifically to work around this - both copy instances must be created while Mirage Mirror is still itself. The model's sequential approach (let the Wonder-copy fully resolve, then try to reactivate Mirror's ability to become a Colossus copy) is not rules-legal, since by that point the permanent no longer possesses that ability. Without this correctly executed, the resulting board only allows for 3 unblockable flying damage plus easily-blocked ground attackers, failing to guarantee lethal damage to the opponent.
model_solution:
1. Tap four lands and cast Hedron Archive ({4}). Let it resolve onto the battlefield.
2. Tap Hedron Archive for {C}{C}, adding 2 mana to your pool (you now have your remaining 2 land mana + these 2 = 4 floating mana total).
3. Cast Metalwork Colossus. Its cost {11} is reduced by the mana value of noncreature artifacts you control: Bomat Bazaar Barge (4) + Mirage Mirror (3) + Hedron Archive (4) = 11, so it costs {0}. Cast it for free; it enters as a 10/10 (summoning sick, which is fine).
4. Activate Mirage Mirror's ability for {2} (from your 4 floating mana), targeting Multiform Wonder. Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Multiform Wonder until end of turn (retaining its own "becomes a copy" ability, per its printed text).
5. While it is a copy of Multiform Wonder, activate "Pay {E}: gains flying/vigilance/lifelink," paying your single energy counter and choosing flying. Mirage Mirror gains flying until end of turn as an independent continuous effect.
6. Activate Mirage Mirror's ability again for your last {2} floating mana, this time targeting Metalwork Colossus. Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Metalwork Colossus (10/10). The "flying until end of turn" effect from step 5 is not a copy effect, so it persists on Mirage Mirror (rule 707.4) — Mirage Mirror is now a 10/10 flying creature. It has been under your control since the start of the turn, so it has no summoning sickness.
7. Proceed to combat and attack with Mirage Mirror (a 10/10 flier). You may also attack with Multiform Wonder and/or crew Bomat Bazaar Barge with the real Metalwork Colossus (crewing ignores summoning sickness) for extra safety, but it isn't required.
8. None of the opponent's creatures (two 4/4 Hollow Ones, one 6/6 Chaos Maw) have flying or reach, so Mirage Mirror cannot be blocked. It deals 10 unblockable combat damage, reducing the opponent from 10 life to 0 and winning the game this turn.
